DZA.note: The article says nothing of e-procurement.
The article names the National Payment Committee under Bank of Algeria Regulation 26-01 but does not describe licensing, a switch or a regional link.
The article says nothing of consumer rules or complaints for digital financial services.
The article names an international card for online purchases abroad but no cross-border corridor or regional system.

facts.fact: Echorouk reports that Algerians can pay public fees and services electronically, among them housing instalments, Hajj fees, insurance and taxes, and that administrative services were 28% of online payment transactions in the first half of 2026.

DZA.note: The article describes payments to government, not government payments to people.
The article cites no survey of adults holding accounts.

facts.fact: Echorouk reports that Algerian banks (CPA, BDL, BNA) offer mobile and QR-code payments for shop purchases and person-to-person transfers, with QR payment transactions up 1,200% in six months per an unnamed report.

systems.owner: CPA, BDL, BNA and other banks

facts.fact: Echorouk reports that electronic channels are being used to pay several public services and fees, among them housing instalments, Hajj fees, insurance and taxes.
